name: Dental Practice / DSO (Dental Service Organization)
description: General or specialty dental practice providing preventive, restorative, cosmetic, and surgical dental care. Suitable for solo private practices, multi-dentist group practices, and DSO (Dental Service Organization) managed practices with centralized administrative support.

org_structure.overview: The dental practice is organized around the clinical team (dentists, hygienists, assistants) providing patient care, supported by front office and business operations. In a DSO model, the practice manager reports to a regional manager while the lead dentist reports to a clinical director — creating a matrix. The model supports general dentistry and/or specialties (orthodontics, endodontics, periodontics, oral surgery, pediatric dentistry). Lab work may be in-house or sent to a commercial dental lab. Revenue cycle focuses on dental insurance (procedure-code based with annual maximums) alongside fee-for-service patients.

departments.name: Practice Leadership
departments.description: Ownership or DSO management and clinical leadership. In solo practices the owner-dentist fills both roles.

roles.title: Owner Dentist / Lead Dentist
roles.description: Clinical oversight, treatment planning, complex case dentistry, and clinical quality. In solo practice, also handles business ownership.

roles.title: Practice Manager
roles.description: Business operations: scheduling, insurance billing, accounts receivable, payroll, supply ordering, staffing, and P&L management. May not exist in very small practices.

roles.title: DSO Regional Manager (multi-site)
roles.description: Oversees multiple practice locations; KPIs on production, collections, patient satisfaction, and staffing. Only present in DSO models.

departments.name: Clinical — Dentistry
departments.description: Dentists providing examination, diagnosis, treatment planning, and dental procedures.

roles.title: General Dentist
roles.description: Comprehensive dental care: exams, fillings, crowns, bridges, extractions, root canals, dentures, and preventive care.

roles.title: Specialist — Orthodontist
roles.description: Braces, clear aligners (Invisalign), and orthognathic treatment planning. Often shared across multiple locations or visits weekly.

roles.title: Specialist — Endodontist
roles.description: Root canal therapy, endodontic retreatment, and microsurgery. Often a visiting specialist.

roles.title: Specialist — Oral Surgeon
roles.description: Tooth extractions (including wisdom teeth), dental implants, bone grafting, and oral pathology biopsy.

roles.title: Specialist — Periodontist
roles.description: Gum disease treatment, scaling/root planing, gum grafts, implant placement, and periodontal maintenance.

roles.title: Specialist — Pediatric Dentist
roles.description: Child and adolescent dentistry; behavior management, sedation, and treatment of pediatric dental disease.

departments.name: Clinical — Dental Hygiene
departments.description: Licensed dental hygienists providing preventive care, periodontal therapy, and patient education.

roles.title: Registered Dental Hygienist (RDH)
roles.description: Prophylaxis, scaling/root planing, periodontal assessments, radiographs, fluoride application, sealants, and oral hygiene instruction.

roles.title: Expanded Functions Dental Assistant (EFDA)
roles.description: Placement of restorative materials, sealants, coronal polishing, and radiography under dentist supervision.

departments.name: Clinical Support — Dental Assisting
departments.description: Dental assistants supporting dentists chairside, sterilizing instruments, and preparing treatment rooms.

roles.title: Certified Dental Assistant (CDA)
roles.description: Chairside assisting during procedures, instrument sterilization, room setup/breakdown, impression taking, and radiographs.

roles.title: Sterilization Technician
roles.description: Instrument processing, sterilization equipment management, infection control compliance, and supply inventory.

departments.name: Dental Lab (In-House)
departments.description: On-site dental laboratory fabricating crowns, bridges, dentures, and orthodontic appliances. Many smaller practices outsource this function.

roles.title: Dental Laboratory Technician
roles.description: Fabricates crowns, bridges, veneers, dentures, partials, and orthodontic models. May specialize in crown/bridge or denture work.

roles.title: Digital Dentistry / CAD-CAM Specialist
roles.description: Operates intraoral scanners, milling machines, and 3D printers for same-day restorations (CEREC) and digital workflow integration.

departments.name: Front Office & Business Operations
departments.description: Patient scheduling, insurance verification, billing, collections, and front-desk patient experience.

roles.title: Front Desk / Patient Coordinator
roles.description: Appointment scheduling, patient check-in/out, insurance verification, benefit explanation, co-pay collection, and phone management.

roles.title: Treatment Plan Coordinator
roles.description: Presents treatment plans and financial arrangements to patients; discusses insurance coverage, payment options, and membership plans.

roles.title: Dental Biller / Insurance Coordinator
roles.description: Dental claim submission (ADA 2015 form), payment posting, insurance follow-up, denial management, patient statements, and aging report management.

roles.title: Marketing / Patient Engagement Coordinator
roles.description: Online reputation, Google reviews, social media, patient recall/reactivation campaigns, new patient acquisition, and community events.

key_relationships: Lead Dentist and Practice Manager are the two poles of the practice — clinical quality and business health. In a DSO, these may be separate reporting lines to the regional clinical director and regional operations manager.
Dentists and Dental Hygienists have interdependent schedules: the dentist performs the exam after the hygiene cleaning, so efficient hygiene-dentist handoff directly impacts production.
Dental Assistants are paired with specific dentists for chairside support; good assistant-dentist teams produce higher quality and volume.
Treatment Plan Coordinator bridges clinical recommendations (from the dentist) and patient financial decisions — a key role for case acceptance.
Front desk and hygiene team coordinate the all-annual-visit scheduling that forms the backbone of a recall-based practice.
Lab technician communicates with dentists on case specifications, material choices, shade matching, and delivery timelines.
Insurance/Billing team works with front desk to verify benefits before the patient is seated — preventing surprise denials and patient dissatisfaction.
